title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 70C or SOCIOL 63 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 193A

title: Seminar in Data Science
description: An introduction to the field of Data Science; intended for entering freshman and transfers.

title: Introduction to Data Science
description: Introduces the full data cycle. Topics include data collection and retrieval, data cleaning, exploratory analysis and visualization, introduction to statistical modeling, inference, and communicating findings. Applications include real data from a wide-range of fields with emphasis on understanding reproducible practices.

title: Basic Statistics
description: Introduces basic inferential statistics including confidence intervals and hypothesis testing on means and proportions, t-distribution, Chi Square, regression and correlation. F-distribution and nonparametric statistics included if time permits.

title: Introduction to Biological Statistics
description: Introductory statistical techniques used to collect and analyze experimental and observational data from health sciences and biology. Includes exploration of data, probability and sampling distributions, basic statistical inference for means and proportions, linear regression, and analysis of variance.

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Computer Science
description: Introduction to the basic concepts of probability and statistics with discussion of applications to computer science.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4

title: Statistical Computing and Exploratory Data Analysis
description: Introduces key concepts in statistical computing. Techniques such as exploratory data analysis, data visualization, simulation, and optimization methods, are presented in the context of data analysis within a statistical computing environment.
prerequisites_raw: ( STATS 7 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3) and ( I&C SCI 31 or I&C SCI H32 )

title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis I
description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing data from experiments and surveys. Methods covered include two-sample procedures, analysis of variance, simple and multiple linear regression.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 7 or STATS 8 or STATS 67 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3 or ( STATS 120A and STATS 120B and STATS 120C )

title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis II
description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing data from surveys or experiments. Emphasizes application and understanding of methods for categorical data including contingency tables, logistic and Poisson regression, loglinear models.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 110

title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis III
description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing longitudinal data from experiments and cohort studies. Topics covered include survival methods for censored time-to-event data, linear mixed models, non-linear mixed effects models, and generalized estimating equations.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 111

title: Introduction to Bayesian Data Analysis
description: Basic Bayesian concepts and methods with emphasis on data analysis. Prior and posterior probability distributions, modeling, and Markov Chain Monte Carlo techniques are presented in the context of data analysis within a statistical computing environment.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 120C . Recommended: STATS 110

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics I
description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Axiomatic definition of probability, random variables, probability distributions, expectation.
prerequisites_raw: ( MATH 2A or AP Calculus AB with a minimum score of 4 or AP Calculus AB Subscore with a minimum score of 4 or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 3) and ( MATH 2B or AP Calculus BC with a minimum score of 4) and ( MATH 2D or MATH 4)

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics II
description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Point and interval estimation, frequentist hypothesis testing, Bayesian inference, limit theorems, simulation, and the bootstrap.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 120A

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics III
description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Power and sample size calculation, Neyman-Pearson lemma, (generalized) likelihood ratio test, one-way ANOVA, two-way ANOVA, simple linear regression and its statistical inference and diagnosis, and multiple linear regression.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 120B and ( MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N )

title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
description: Theory and application of multivariate statistical methods. Topics include statistical inference for the multivariate normal model and its extensions to multiple samples and regression, use of statistical packages for data visualization and reduction, discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, and factor analysis.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 120C and ( MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N )

title: Project in Data Science I
description: Problem definition and analysis, data representation, algorithm selection, solution validation, and results presentation. Students do team projects and lectures cover analysis alternatives, project planning, and data analysis issues. First quarter emphasizes approach selection, project planning, and experimental design.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 68 and SWE 43 and COMPSCI 122A and COMPSCI 178 and I&C SCI 46 and STATS 111

title: Project in Data Science II
description: Problem definition and analysis, data representation, algorithm selection, solution validation, and results presentation. Students do team projects and lectures cover analysis alternatives, project planning, and data analysis issues. Second quarter emphasizes project execution and analysis, and presentation of results.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 170A and STATS 112 . In Progress (IP) grade for STATS 170A is also accepted

title: Honors Research
description: Directed independent research in Statistics for ICS honors and Campuswide Honors Collegium students.

title: Individual Study
description: Individual research or investigations under the direction of an individual faculty member.

title: Intermediate Probability and Statistical Theory
description: Basics of probability theory, random variables and basic transformations, univariate distributions—discrete and continuous, multivariate distributions.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 120C with a minimum grade of B-

title: Intermediate Probability and Statistical Theory
description: Random samples, transformations, limit laws, normal distribution theory, introduction to stochastic processes, data reduction, point estimation (maximum likelihood).
prerequisites_raw: STATS 200A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Intermediate Probability and Statistical Theory
description: Interval estimation, hypothesis testing, decision theory and Bayesian inference, basic linear model theory.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 200B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis I
description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing data from experiments and surveys. Methods covered include two-sample procedures, analysis of variance, simple and multiple linear regression.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 7 or STATS 8

title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis II
description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing data from surveys or experiments. Emphasizes application and understanding of methods for categorical data including contingency tables, logistic and Poisson regression, loglinear models.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 201 with a minimum grade of B- or STATS 210 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Statistical Methods for Data Analysis III
description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing longitudinal data from experiments and cohort studies. Topics covered include survival methods for censored time-to-event data, linear mixed models, non-linear mixed effects models, and generalized estimating equations.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 202 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Introduction to Bayesian Data Analysis
description: Basic Bayesian concepts and methods with emphasis on data analysis. Special emphasis on specification of prior distributions. Development for one-two samples and on to binary, Poisson and linear regression. Analyses performed using free OpenBugs software.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 120C . Recommended: STATS 201 or STATS 210

title: Bayesian Data Analysis
description: Covers basic Bayesian concepts and methods with emphasis on data analysis. Special emphasis on specification of prior distributions. Development of methods and theory for one and two samples, binary, Poisson, and linear regression.
prerequisites_raw: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B and DATA 210P with a minimum grade of B

title: Statistical Methods I: Linear Models
description: Statistical methods for analyzing data from surveys and experiments. Topics include randomization and model-based inference, two-sample methods, analysis of variance, linear regression and model diagnostics.
prerequisites_raw: Knowledge of basic statistics, calculus, linear algebra

title: Statistical Methods I: Linear Models
description: Statistical methods for analyzing data from surveys and experiments. Topics include randomization and model-based inference, two-sample methods, analysis of variance, linear regression, and model diagnostics.
prerequisites_raw: Knowledge of basic statistics (at the level of STATS 7 ), calculus, and linear algebra

title: Statistical Methods II: Categorical Data
description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing discrete and non-normal outcomes. Emphasizes the development and application of methods for categorical data, including contingency tables, logistic and Poisson regression, loglinear models.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 210 with a minimum grade of B-. May not be taken for graduate credit by Ph.D. students in Statistics

title: Statistical Methods III: Longitudinal Data
description: Introduction to statistical methods for analyzing longitudinal outcomes. Emphasizes the development and application of regression methods for correlated and censored outcomes. Methods for continuous and discrete correlated outcomes, as well as censored outcomes, are covered.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 210B with a minimum grade of B-. May not be taken for graduate credit by Ph.D. students in Statistics

title: Statistical Methods II: Generalized Linear Models
description: Development of the theory and application of generalized linear models. Topics include likelihood estimation and asymptotic distributional theory for exponential families, quasi-likelihood and mixed model development. Emphasizes methodological development and application to real scientific problems.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 210 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B-

title: Statistical Methods III: Methods for Correlated Data
description: Development and application of statistical methods for analyzing corrected data. Topics covered include repeated measures ANOVA, linear mixed models, non-linear mixed effects models, and generalized estimating equations. Emphasizes both theoretical development and application of the presented methodology.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 211 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Probability and Statistics Topics
description: Advanced topics in probability and statistical inference including measure theoretic probability, large sample theory, decision theory, resampling and Monte Carlo methods, nonparametric methods.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 200C with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Probability and Statistics Topics
description: Advanced topics in probability and statistical inference, including measure theoretic probability, large sample theory, decision theory, resampling and Monte Carlo methods, nonparametric methods.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 220A with a minimum grade of B- and MATH 140B

title: Bayesian Statistical Analysis
description: Introduction to the Bayesian approach to statistical inference. Topics include univariate and multivariate models, choice of prior distributions, hierarchical models, computation including Markov chain Monte Carlo, model checking, and model selection.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 205 with a minimum grade of B- and STATS 230 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Statistical Computing Methods
description: Numerical computations and algorithms with applications in statistics. Topics include optimization methods including the EM algorithm, random number generation and simulation, Markov chain simulation tools, and numerical integration.
prerequisites_raw: Two quarters of upper-division or graduate training in probability and statistics

title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
description: Theory and application of multivariate statistical methods. Topics include statistical inference for the multivariate normal model and its extensions to multiple samples and regression, use of statistical packages for data visualization and reduction, discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, and factor analysis.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 120C and ( MATH 3A or I&C SCI 6N )

title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
description: Theory and application of multivariate statistical methods. Topics include statistical inference for the multivariate normal model and its extensions to multiple samples and regression, use of statistical packages for data visualization and dimension reduction, discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, factor analysis.
prerequisites_raw: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B- and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B-

title: Time Series Analysis
description: Statistical models for time series. Topics include linear models for trends; stationary time-series; non-stationary time series; forecasting and Kalman filtering; time-series smoothing; seasonal models; ARCH, GARCH and stochastic volatility models; multivariate time series; vector autoregressive models; spectral analysis; case studies.
prerequisites_raw: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B- and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B-

title: Theory and Practice of Sample Survey
description: Basic techniques and statistical methods for designing surveys and analyzing collected survey data. Topics include simple random sampling, ratio and regression estimates, stratified sampling, cluster sampling, sampling with unequal probabilities, multistage sampling, and methods to handle nonresponse.
prerequisites_raw: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B

title: Causal Inference
description: Various approaches to causal inference focusing on the Rubin causal model and propensity-score methods. Topics include randomized experiments, observational studies, non-compliance, ignorable and non-ignorable treatment assignment, instrumental variables, and sensitivity analysis. Applications from economics, politics, education, and medicine.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 200C with a minimum grade of B- and STATS 210 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Stochastic Processes
description: Introduction to the theory and application of stochastic processes. Topics include Markov chains, continuous-time Markov processes, Poisson processes, and Brownian motion. Applications include Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and financial modeling (for example, option pricing).
prerequisites_raw: STATS 120C

title: Stochastic Processes
description: Introduction to the theory and application of stochastic processes. Topics include Poisson processes, Markov chains, continuous-time Markov processes, and Brownian motion. Applications include Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and financial modeling (e.g. option pricing).
prerequisites_raw: DATA 200AP with a minimum grade of B and DATA 200BP with a minimum grade of B

title: Statistical Consulting
description: Training in collaborative research and practical application of statistics. Emphasis on effective communication as it relates to identifying scientific objectives, formulating a statistical analysis plan, choice of statistical methods, and interpretation of results and their limitations to non-statisticians.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 203 with a minimum grade of B or STATS 212 with a minimum grade of B or STATS 210C with a minimum grade of B

title: Seminar in Statistics
description: Periodic seminar series covering topics of current research in statistics and its application.

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics I
description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Axiomatic definition of probability, random variables, probability distributions, expectation.

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics II
description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Point estimation, interval estimating, and testing hypotheses, Bayesian approaches to inference.

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics III
description: Introduction to basic principles of probability and statistical inference. Contingency table analysis, linear regression, analysis of variance, model checking.

title: Special Topics in Statistics
description: Studies in selected areas of statistics. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Thesis Supervision
description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.

title: Introduction to Software Engineering
description: Concepts, methods, and current practice of software engineering. Large-scale software production, software life cycle models, principles, and techniques for each stage of development.
prerequisites_raw: I&C SCI 32 or I&C SCI H32 or I&C SCI 32A

title: Requirements Analysis and Engineering
description: Equips students to develop techniques of software-intensive systems through successful requirements analysis techniques and requirements engineering. Students learn systematic process of developing requirements through cooperative problem analysis, representation, and validation.
prerequisites_raw: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C and SWE 43 with a minimum grade of C

title: Software Testing, Analysis, and Quality Assurance
description: Preparation for developing high-quality software through successful veriﬁcation and validation techniques. Fundamental principles of software testing, implementing software testing practices, ensuring the thoroughness of testing to gain conﬁdence in the correctness of the software.
prerequisites_raw: ( I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 46 with a minimum grade of C) and SWE 43 with a minimum grade of C

title: Project in Software System Design
description: Specification, design, construction, testing, and documentation of a complete software system. Special emphasis on the need for and use of teamwork, careful planning, and other techniques for working with large systems.
prerequisites_raw: SWE 43 and I&C SCI 33

title: Engineering Artificial Intelligence Software
description: Design, deploy, and manage software incorporating AI components in real-world production environments. Topics include types of models, in-house vs. third-party models, retrieval augmented generation, fine-tuning, prompt engineering, model testing, and reliability.
prerequisites_raw: ( I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C) and ( STATS 7 or STATS 67 )

title: Software Design: Applications
description: Introduction to application design: designing the overall functionality of a software application. Topics include general design theory, software design theory, and software architecture. Includes practice in designing and case studies of existing designs.
prerequisites_raw: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C or GDIM 33 with a minimum grade of C

title: Software Design: Structure and Implementation
description: Introduction to implementation design: designing the internals of a software application. Topics include design aesthetics, design implementation, design recovery, design patterns, and component reuse. Includes practice in designing and case studies of existing designs.
prerequisites_raw: I&C SCI 45J or I&C SCI 46

title: Internet Applications Engineering
description: Concepts in Internet applications engineering with emphasis on the Web. Peer-to-Peer and Interoperability. Topics include HTTP and REST, Remote Procedure/Method Calls, Web Services, data representations, content distribution networks, identity management, relevant W3C/IETF standards, and relevant new large-scale computing styles.
prerequisites_raw: ( COMPSCI 132 or EECS 148 ) and I&C SCI 45J

title: Information Retrieval
description: An introduction to information retrieval including indexing, retrieval, classifying, and clustering text and multimedia documents.
prerequisites_raw: ( I&C SCI 45C with a minimum grade of C or I&C SCI 45J with a minimum grade of C) and ( STATS 7 or STATS 67 or MGMT 7 or AP Statistics with a minimum score of 3)

title: Software Engineering
description: Study of the concepts, methods, and tools for the analysis, design, construction, and measurement of complex software-intensive systems. Underlying principles emphasized. State-of-the-art software engineering and promising research areas covered, including project management.

title: Analysis of Programming Languages
description: Concepts in modern programming languages, their interaction, and the relationship between programming languages and methods for large-scale, extensible software development. Empirical analysis of programming language usage.

title: Program Analysis
description: Covers principles and concepts of automated program analysis. Topics include program representations; intra-procedural data-flow analysis; call-graph construction; pointer analysis; alias analysis; inter-procedural analysis; inter-procedural finite distributive subset problems; inter-procedural distributive environment problems; symbolic execution; and program-analysis applications.

title: Dynamic Analysis, Testing, and Debugging
description: Studies techniques for developing confidence in software from traditional testing techniques to state-of-the-art dynamic analysis and debugging techniques. Emphasis is on assisting developer comprehension of runtime behavior.

title: Software Architecture
description: Study of the concepts, representation techniques, development methods, and tools for architecture-centric software engineering. Topics include domain-specific software architectures, architectural styles, architecture description languages, software connectors, and dynamism in architectures.

title: Information Retrieval, Filtering, and Classification
description: Algorithms for the storage, retrieval, filtering, and classification of textual and multimedia data. The vector space model, Boolean and probabilistic queries, and relevance feedback. Latent semantic indexing; collaborative filtering; and relationship to machine learning methods.
prerequisites_raw: COMPSCI 161 and COMPSCI 171 and ( I&C SCI 6N or MATH 3A or MATH 6G)

title: Intelligent User Interfaces
description: Explores example software systems and their underlying concepts that leverage computing to empower and augment human individuals in their activities. Topics span the fields of user interface design, human-computer interaction, software engineering, and cognitive computing.
prerequisites_raw: COMPSCI 171

title: Human Aspects of Software Engineering
description: Selected topics about the cooperative and human aspects of software engineering from the perspective that software engineering is inherently an endeavor involving human stakeholders. Topics may include but are not limited to collaboration, trust, creativity, well-being, productivity, and software tools.

title: Data Structures
description: Exploration of well-known data structures to represent computational problems. Topics include linked lists, graphs, binary trees, stacks, queues, heaps, and hash tables, among others.

title: Algorithms
description: Exploration of strategies to tackle computational problems whose solutions include well-known algorithms. Topics include sorting, searching, and indexing, among others.

title: Network Programming
description: Exploration of networking principles and concepts for the development of distributed software. Topics include programming against well-known network protocols, ports and sockets, and network APIs.

title: Database Programming
description: Exploration of software development with substantial reliance on a database for storage and retrieval of data. Topics include relational databases, structured query language, relational database management systems, APIs and libraries for database programming, among others.

title: Concurrent Programming
description: Exploration of concepts and mechanisms for the development of concurrent software. Topics include threads, locks, race conditions, and deadlocks, among others.

title: GUI Programming
description: Exploration of interactive software with substantial graphical user interface elements. Topics include libraries and frameworks for GUI programming, layout design and alternatives, event-driven programming, among others.

title: Mobile Programming
description: Exploration of contemporary libraries and frameworks for construction of mobile applications. Topics include emulators, mobile development standards and patterns, energy consumption issues, screen layout, among others.

title: Applied Information Retrieval
description: Exploration of principles and concepts for textual information retrieval. Topics include tokenization, inverted indexes, scored retrieval, and precision and recall.

title: Neural Network Programming
description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and processes for training and using deep neural networks for classification problems. Topics include tensors and tensor operations, gradient-based optimization, feature engineering and learning, and workflow of learning systems.

title: Applied Data Analytics
description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and processes used in supervised and unsupervised learning for classification and clustering, from a software engineering perspective. Topics include K-Nearest Neighbors, Logistic Regression, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, K-Means, and model assessment.

title: Web Programming
description: Exploration of the concepts, terminology, and popular frameworks for developing full-stack web applications. Students develop simple applications using multiple development stacks, and deploy them on the cloud.

title: Introduction to Large Language Models
description: Introduces LLMs for software engineering, covering transformers, prompt/context engineering, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Students gain hands-on experience interacting with models using APIs and open-source models while laying the foundation for advanced study in SWE 270P .

title: Software Testing and Debugging
description: Designed to teach students how to ensure high-quality software by means of testing, debugging, and other quality assurance activities. Students learn a combination of both theoretical and practical skills, including hands-on experience with modern tools and approaches.

title: Advanced Programming Techniques
description: Teaches students the various ways software can be decomposed and then how to put the parts back together. Students are exposed to a variety of different programming styles and composition mechanisms.

title: User Experience and Interaction
description: Provides an introduction to the basic principles of human-computer interaction (HCI) and the pragmatic aspects of usability engineering. Topics include the fundamentals of interaction, user experience, design for usability, and evaluation of products for their usability.

title: Distributed Software Architecture
description: Study of software system architectures and architectural styles for large-scale distributed applications, and contemporary technologies and standards for their construction. Topics include client-server, peer-to-peer, publish-subscribe, REST, cloud computing, content distribution networks, scalability, latency, caching, and security, among others.

title: Reverse Engineering and Modeling
description: Introduces theories, concepts, representations, techniques, and case studies in understanding large-scale, complex software systems. Topics include static and dynamic modeling notations, manual and (semi-)automated reverse engineering techniques, APIs, patterns, and styles. A significant, hands-on project is included.

title: Software Security and Dependability
description: Principles and concepts for the design and construction of secure software. Topics include common types of software security vulnerabilities, methods for detecting vulnerabilities, design and process methodologies to improve security of software, and techniques for assessing security properties of software.

title: Cloud and Security Foundations
description: Cloud and security foundations provides students fundamental design and security principles about cloud computing and information security. Topics include cloud concepts and architectures; cloud security; data protection and privacy compliance and governance; and security by design, amongst other topics.

title: Engineering Artificial Intelligence Software
description: Design, deploy, and manage software incorporating AI components in real-world production environments. Topics include learning about different types of models, in-house vs. third-party models, retrieval augmented generation, fine-tuning, prompt engineering, model testing, and reliability.

title: Curricular Practical Training
description: Mandatory internship in which students individually work at an outside organization to gain experience with the challenges involved in the practice of software engineering.

title: Capstone Project in Software Engineering
description: Quarter-long software-intensive project focusing on the design and implementation of a novel software system. Students are expected to bring to bear the concepts acquired during the program.

title: Capstone Project in Software Engineering II
description: Focuses on designing and implementing a novel software system. Students work on their project while emphasizing communication skills in business and technical settings. Students practice presenting project ideas, developing portfolios.

title: Research Seminar
description: Forum for presentation and criticism by students of research work in progress. Presentation of problem areas and related work. Specific goals and progress of research.

title: Advisement
description: Mandatory weekly meetings with a faculty advisor.

title: Special Topics in Software Engineering
description: Studies in selected areas of software engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Thesis Supervision
description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparation for the M.S. thesis option or the dissertation requirements for the Ph.D. program.

title: Individual Study
description: Individual research or investigation under the direction of an individual faculty member.

title: Washington DC Internship
description: Supervised internship (20-40 hours per week) in Washington DC government, nonprofit, or private institution consistent with student's interest.
prerequisites_raw: Selected for Washington DC Center Program

title: Washington-Themed Seminar
description: UCDC core course (multiple topics offered each quarter). Enhances students' experiential learning and imparts knowledge and skills to help them transition into public service/private sector positions. One core course per quarter mandatory for all participants in Washington DC Center Program.
prerequisites_raw: Must be selected for Washington DC Center Program

title: Student Participation
description: Campus projects with a University department to enrich academic growth and development as well as academic growth and development of UCI. Includes 30 hours per quarter working on proposed project under faculty/staff supervision. Paper required.
prerequisites_raw: Project must be approved by a Student Affairs Department head and the instructor

title: Student Participation
description: Campus projects with a University department to enrich academic growth and development as well as academic growth and development of UCI. Includes 30 hours per quarter working on proposed project under faculty/staff supervision. Paper required.
prerequisites_raw: UNI AFF 1A

title: Freshman Experience
description: An introduction to the freshman experience provides an overview of the University's aims and resources and exploration of developmental theories and skills necessary for academic success. Attention is also paid to questions of personal development and major choice. Materials Fee

title: Mini-Seminars
description: Designed primarily for freshmen as introduction to scholarly inquiry. Each section is taught by a faculty member from one of the academic disciplines and presents interesting and challenging topics representing the instructor's interest. Students participate in discussions, presentations, and projects.

title: UTeach: Student-Taught Seminar
description: Student-taught seminar courses on selected topics. Topics vary each year according to the interest of the students teaching the classes.

title: Introduction to Civic and Community Engagement and Community Research
description: Provides a foundation for understanding the role of public scholarship, civic engagement, and social action, and the relationship between service learning and engaged citizenship. Introduces key theoretical and research methodologies on the traditions and innovations of civic and community engagement.

title: Student Leadership Institute for Climate Resilience
description: An overview of some of the major challenges and opportunities we face in building community climate resilience, as well as tools for action.

title: Introduction to Free Speech and Academic Freedom
description: An introduction to the principles of free speech and academic freedom with a focus on the public university context. Attention is paid to the historical evolution of the central concepts as well as real-world case studies.

title: Intercollegiate Athletics Seminar
description: Designed to provide first-year student-athletes a thorough overview of university life and to help ease their transition into higher education. Ensures that students are successful throughout their time at UC Irvine by developing

title: Intercollegiate Athletics Seminar
description: Designed to provide first-year student-athletes a thorough overview of university life and to help ease their transition into higher education. Ensures that students are successful throughout their time at UC Irvine.

title: Critical Thinking, Ethics, and Just Communities I
description: Part of a three-course series; focuses on expanding critical thinking, developing personal ethics, understanding diversity, equity, and inclusion in on-campus residential communities.

title: Critical Thinking, Ethics, and Just Communities II
description: Part of a three-course series; focuses on expanding critical thinking, developing personal ethics, understanding diversity, equity, and inclusion in on-campus residential communities.

title: Thinking, Ethics, and Just Communities III
description: Part of a three-course series; focuses on expanding critical thinking, developing personal ethics, understanding diversity, equity, and inclusion in on-campus residential communities.

title: Introduction to Startups
description: Entrepreneurship intro course that merges academic rigor with real-world business insights, offering skill-based training in ideation, networking, leadership, team building, finance, and startup founding.

title: Introduction to Research
description: Assists incoming first years (freshmen and transfer students) in their understanding of research opportunities at UCI and how to get involved with faculty-mentored labs and creative projects; covers the necessary knowledge, skills, and resources regarding how to conduct research.

title: Thrive in Research
description: Second of a two-part series designed to assist incoming first years (freshmen and transfer students) in their understanding of research and research opportunities at UCI. Students learn how to get involved with faculty-mentored labs and creative projects.

title: Critical Analysis of Health Science Literature
description: Focuses on evaluation of scientific literature. Aspects of scientific inquiry include scientific method, scientific research design, statistical analysis, and publication processes. Addresses why scientific inquiry cannot be separated from sociocultural influences and concerns. Examples drawn from research on health-related issues.

title: Environmental Issues Affecting the Sustainability of Societies I
description: Focuses on several environmental challenges facing the world today, and explores the problem, possible solutions, and their scientific, technical, and social constraints. Models for systems, their assumptions, predictive uncertainty, and interpretation, play a large role.
prerequisites_raw: UNI STU H30A with a minimum grade of C

title: Environmental Issues Affecting the Sustainability of Societies II
description: Focuses on how we can use Earth’s resources, e.g., food and water, in a more sustainable way, exploring their scientific, technical, and social constraints.
prerequisites_raw: UNI STU H30B with a minimum grade of C

title: Social Science Perspectives on the Sustainability of Societies
description: Introduces the perspectives of social science using examples from different countries to explore how social issues regarding sustainability are influenced by a society’s changing economic and political institutions, and how economic, political, and other social choices affect their sustainability.
prerequisites_raw: EARTHSS H30C with a minimum grade of C

title: Cities: Focal Point for Sustainability Problems and Solutions I
description: Explores the nature of cities, focusing on the challenges facing cities today, their possible solutions, and the technical and social constraints on those solutions.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H30D

title: Cities: Focal Point for Sustainability Problems and Solutions II
description: Explores the nature of cities, focusing on the challenges facing cities today, their possible solutions, and the technical and social constraints on those solutions.
prerequisites_raw: UPPP H30E

title: Topics in Illuminations
description: This course connects students to Illuminations, the Chancellor’s Arts and Culture Initiative. Students will attend five Illuminations-sponsored events and engage in brief preparatory and reflective activities in response to these events.

title: Graduate School Opportunities and Preparation
description: Explores the opportunities associated with graduate school by considering a wide range of disciplines and career paths. Reviews professional and academic paths in graduate school and the ways to prepare for a chosen path.

title: Neurodivergent
description: Examines the evolution of the diagnosis of autism through history. Deep inquiry of the neuroscience, etiology, and genetics of neurodivergent individuals as well as a review of the validity of the varied treatments will inform critical thinking.

title: Pathways to University Success
description: Helps first-year students transition to UC Irvine and promotes a successful University experience. Students learn about academic resources and programs that support acclimation to the campus and enhance academic development through lectures, discussions, and a range of co-curricular activities.

title: Bridges to University Success
description: Helps first-year students transition to UC Irvine and promotes a successful University experience. Students learn about academic resources/programs that support acclimation to the campus and enhance academic development through lectures, writing laboratories, discussions, and a range of co-curricular activities.

title: Leading from Within
description: Students examine characteristics and behaviors of effective leaders. Study the history and theoretical framework for understanding effective leadership. In addition, examine their own leadership strengths and weaknesses and become familiar with the theory behind and use of comprehensive self-assessment tools.

title: Leading Others
description: Students examine best practices within a team environment. They learn goal setting, diagnosing performance problems, designing solutions, and recognizing relevant differences in culture, priorities, and values within a team through lectures, writing, discussions, and practical activities.

title: Leading Change
description: Focused on a global viewpoint, students learn the theoretical framework behind innovation and change management. Develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges, design strategies to bring an expansive vision into fruition, and learn to communicate a vision and strategies.

title: Leadership and Aikido
description: Covers practical applications of theories of leadership, communication, and self-efficacy through lessons in Aikido, personal reflection, and current articles. Focuses on skills that support academic and professional success.

title: Navigating Your UCI Journey: Foundations for Success
description: Provides all incoming students with a core experience focused on building a solid foundation for academic success. Recognizes students' different backgrounds and is designed around modules that support academic success.

title: Strategies for Success
description: Develops students' study skills for general education requirement courses through instruction, small group activities, and application assignments. Topics include goal setting, note taking, examination preparation, memory and concentration, and learning best practices.

title: Doing Research in the Community
description: Critically reimagines the research endeavor and its participants/outcomes. Grapples with methods, values, and relationships involved in research. Explores alternative conceptions of research; focus is community-based. Students work in teams on real-world community research projects with faculty mentors and community partners.
prerequisites_raw: UNI STU 10

title: Special Topics in Campuswide Honors Education
description: Topics in honors education vary depending on the interest of the instructor.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement is recommended

title: Philanthropy in the Community
description: Introduces the role of community engagement, social action and philanthropy. Examines theories and practices of philanthropy, and strategies for social change. Involves hand-on engagement with philanthropy in the form of students making decisions about the distribution of a real fund.

title: Advanced Internship in Undergraduate Education
description: Advanced interns have a year's internship experience and return to contribute to Undergraduate Education programs in a leadership position. Students work three-five hours per week in a DUE office to coordinate or lead less-experienced interns and/or events.
prerequisites_raw: UNI AFF 1A and UNI AFF 1B and UNI AFF 1C

title: Peer Tutoring Methods and Applications
description: Overview and readings in research-based principles of learning for all undergraduate tutors. Tutors receive instruction, practice, and evaluation in effective communication strategies, learning development, cultural competencies, and 1:1 facilitation. Taken concurrently when serving as a tutor in any department.

title: Methods and Application in Small Group Instruction
description: Explores various theories and methods of learning and development and their practical application in small group settings. Peer tutors receive instruction in the design, implementation, and evaluation of an effective learning environment for undergraduate students.

title: Pedagogy of Small Group Facilitation - LAs
description: Overview and readings in evidence-based instruction for undergraduate learning assistants. LAs receive instruction, training, and feedback on effective small group facilitation and active learning. To be taken while serving as a learning assistant in a course.

title: Campuswide Honors Thesis Seminar
description: Supports the honors thesis research activities of Campuswide Honors Collegium students. Students set research goals, discuss, and develop their research interests.

title: Campuswide Honors Thesis Seminar
description: Supports the honors thesis research activities of Campuswide Honors Collegium students. Students work with each other to improve both written and spoken presentations of their results.
prerequisites_raw: UNI STU H176A

title: Mentored Learning Assistant Field Work
description: Oversight of trained learning assistants by the course instructor, including training in the discipline and responsibilities associated with supporting active group work. Instructor mentors LAs in how assisting small groups supports their career goals.

title: Teaching Seminar: Theory and Practice
description: For students selected to be discussion leaders for University Studies 1. Models of teaching, developmental theory applied to college freshmen, curriculum development. Practice of teaching techniques and group management skills.

title: Group Project for Discussion Leaders
description: For discussion leaders for University Studies 1. Weekly discussion group training for leading effective groups in addition to evaluations of weekly discussion sections and completion of a special project on issues of freshman development. Materials Fee

title: Internship
description: Enables students from all majors to receive credit for an approved internship on or off-campus. Internship sites may be public or private, for profit or non-profit agencies, organizations, companies, or corporations offering paid or unpaid learning experiences.

title: Directed Studies in Undergraduate Education
description: Students do directed study (research, readings, etc.) on a topic related to Undergraduate Education under the supervision of one of the faculty who serve as Deans or Faculty Directors in the Division of Undergraduate Education.

title: UTeach Special Study
description: Students accepted to teach a UTeach course in spring quarter enroll in Special or Independent Study with their faculty mentor during the preceding fall quarter to develop their detailed course syllabus.

title: UTeach: Teaching Theory and Practice
description: Students accepted to teach a UTeach course in spring quarter enroll during the winter to develop their teaching skills in preparation for teaching the following quarter.
prerequisites_raw: UNI STU 197A

title: UTeach: Teaching Practicum
description: Students selected to teach in the UTeach Program teach their courses and meet weekly in a seminar to continue to develop and enhance their teaching skills.
prerequisites_raw: UNI STU 197B

title: Study Abroad Experiential Learning
description: Study abroad on an approved program. Complete critical reflection (written paper, blog, etc.) submitted no later than the end of the quarter following the completion of the study abroad program. Enroll while studying abroad or the quarter immediately following return.

title: Reflections While Abroad
description: For students while they are studying abroad; maximizing learning outcomes by critically reflecting on learning experiences while abroad. Topics include cultural observations, professional issues, cultural competence, etc. Participants are located in different countries around the world.

title: Internship Plus
description: Provides training and development of career readiness competencies in parallel with a student’s internship experience. Internship sites may be public or private, for profit or non-profit agencies, organizations, companies, or corporations offering paid or unpaid learning experiences.

title: NIH Fellowship Writing Skills
description: Designed for graduate students in biomedical science departments who are preparing to write applications for NRSA (F30/F31) fellowships from the NIH. It involves a mixture of lectures, panel discussions, and peer review of writing samples.

title: California Community College Internship
description: The California Community College Internship offers graduate students the opportunity to learn about faculty life, governance, and teaching at local community colleges. Structures fieldwork for students to participate in and reflect on the educational mission of community colleges.
prerequisites_raw: Teaching experience

title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.

title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.
prerequisites_raw: UNI STU 390A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Pedagogy and Academic Job Preparation
description: Focuses on advanced pedagogical research and practices. Students design and implement an integrated curriculum in the context of the TA Professional Development Program. Prepare for the academic job market by developing application materials and reviewing Pedagogical Fellow applicants.
prerequisites_raw: UNI STU 390B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Introduction to Urban Studies
description: Introduces the substantive areas, concepts, and tools in the field of urban studies. Acquaints students with physical, environmental, social, economic, and political dimensions of cities. Examines the challenges facing cities, including poverty, sustainability, development, globalization, and others.

title: Introduction to Urban Planning and Policy
description: Introduces students to the basic issues in urban planning and public policy.

title: Introduction to Environmental Analysis and Design
description: Overview of general concepts, theoretical principles, and analytical techniques for investigating environmental systems. Integrates tools from natural and social sciences to analyze contemporary environmental challenges such as pollution, resource acquisition, facility and ecosystem design, impact assessments, formulation of environmental policy.

title: Cities, Communities, and Urban Problems
description: Overview of theoretical, substantive, and policy issues in urban sociology. History of urbanization, the school of human ecology, and recent trends regarding urbanism. Time is devoted to understanding the causes and possible solutions to urban problems.

title: Introduction to Labor Studies
description: Introduces students to various aspects of labor and employment relations in the U.S., including the perspective of working people and their collective labor organizations. Analyzes changes in employment trends and the changing nature of work.

title: The Green New Deal
description: Introduces students to the basic motivations and history behind policies collectively known as “The Green New Deal.” Students learn about large-scale models for equitable growth and sustainability and the politics of implementing them in the U.S. and internationally.

title: The Power of Music and Social Change
description: Introduces students to the emerging science of music and its remarkable power in shaping our lives, from individual flourishing and social change to higher education, careers, and connections with nature.

title: Special Topics in Urban Studies
description: Course content varies with interest of the instructor.

title: History of Cities
description: Surveys the global and historical co-evolution of cities and social institutions, including religion, the economy, governance, the arts, technology, and family life.

title: Urban Inequality
description: Examines structural inequality and the influence that urbanization has in affecting race, ethnic, and class relations. Explores how race/ethnicity, class, urban space, housing, economic development, public education, and land policy intersect in cities, both historically and today.

title: Comparative Approaches to Urban Regions
description: An introduction to comparative urbanization in developing countries. Introduces students to the geography, history, and theories of urbanization, and then reviews urban planning, public policy, and governance.

title: Race in the City: Past, Present, and Future
description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.

title: Urban and Regional Planning
description: Important substantive areas, concepts, tools in the field of urban and regional planning. Topics include: forces that have historically guided and are currently guiding U.S. urbanization; land use, economic development, housing and community development, environmental planning; legal, environmental, governmental contexts.

title: Cities and Transportation
description: The relationship between urban areas and transportation systems. Economic analysis of cities, transportation and urban form, highway congestion, environmental impacts of transportation, public transit, land use and transportation, and political influences on transportation planning.

title: Housing and Urban Development Policy
description: Surveys public policy issues and develops analytic techniques in the areas of housing and urban development. Examines a range of policy topics including housing assistance to low- and moderate-income families, housing finance system, incentives for economic development, and neighborhood preservation.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Previous course work in economics

title: Urban Economic Development Policy
description: Theoretical and practical perspectives on local economic development policy. Integrates economic, planning, and political perspectives. Overview of economic role of cities and metropolitan areas. Specific development issues include: link between taxes, regulation, job growth; redevelopment planning; evaluation economic development policy.

title: Climate Solutions
description: Introduction to climate change science and impacts on the health of people and the planet with a focus on the multi-dimensional aspects of solutions to the climate crisis.

title: Foundations of Community Health
description: A social ecological framework for understanding community health is presented. Measures of individual and community health are compared, and the influence of personal and environmental factors on individual, group, and population health is examined. Community health promotion strategies are discussed.

title: Poverty and Change in Developing Countries
description: Focuses on poverty in developing countries. Analyzes the magnitude and changing nature of poverty in the global south. Critically examines poverty conceptualized in terms of economic deprivation, well-being, and social exclusion.

title: Advanced Research Methods
description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Global Poverty and Inequality in the 21st Century
description: Explores a multidisciplinary understanding of poverty and inequality in the 21st century and assesses impact of education, health, technology, and other interventions. Course offered online only.

title: Cities and Climate Change
description: Students examine the intersection between climate change and social justice while developing skills necessary for local climate action, such as inventorying emissions, assessing vulnerability, and evaluating the costs, benefits, and equity implications of mitigation and adaptation strategies.

title: Environmental Justice
description: Engages students to critically analyze and evaluate environmental problems, environmental responses, and planning and policy debates regarding "environmental justice" - essentially the race, class, and equity implications of environmental problems and policies.

title: Gentrification
description: Gentrification is a complex process that changes the makeup of neighborhoods and fuels political and policy conflicts. Students are provided with tools to understand the process and conceive of policies to ensure more inclusive and equitable cities.

title: Human Trafficking: Prevention, Protection, Prosecution, Policy, and Partnership
description: Equips students with a deeper understanding of human trafficking, and explores their role in ending the fastest-growing criminal industry worldwide: the exploitation of human beings through the use of force, fraud, or coercion.

title: Introduction to GIS for Planning and Policy
description: Provides hands-on experience creating, visualizing, and interpreting spatial data, with a focus on Geographic Information Systems (GIS) applications for urban planning and public policy.

title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
description: Provides hands-on experience using geoprocessing to analyze spatial data and using maps to visualize and communicate findings, with a focus on Geographic Information Systems (GIS) applications for urban planning and public policy.
prerequisites_raw: UPPP 120 with a minimum grade of C-

title: Spatial Analysis Project
description: As the capstone in the Geographic Information Systems (GIS) degree specialization, students are guided through the process of applying their GIS skills to designing and conducting an original spatial research project, focusing on research design and research methods.
prerequisites_raw: UPPP 120 with a minimum grade of C- and UPPP 125 with a minimum grade of C-

title: American Public Policy
description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

title: Environmental Sustainability I
description: Provides an introduction to sustainability from different points of view; historical, scientific, political, ethical, and economic.

title: Energy Justice and Just Transitions
description: Investigates how sustainability can be implemented in a variety of contexts including water, energy, non-renewable resources, biodiversity, and urban policy, and also how it could be measured.

title: Environmental Law and Policy
description: Environmental law as a combination of traditional legal principles and newly created statutes, rules, and decisions applied to environmental protection. Investigates roles of courts, legislature, executive branch and administrative agencies, and private citizens attempting to regulate environmental quality.

title: Urban Data Science
description: Introduces computational tools, data literacy, spatial analysis methods, and introductory statistics for understanding cities and metropolitan regions.

title: Global Metropolis
description: Explores global perspectives on urban phenomena like poverty and housing, postcolonial and global-South urbanization, citizenship, race, violence, inequality, and our shared climate future.

title: Environmental Hazards in an Urbanizing World
description: Development patterns, including urbanization, can contribute to environmental hazard severity. Humans can plan, mitigate, and prepare to reduce costly hazard losses. Students learn about environmental hazards and human response to these threats.

title: Environmental Governance
description: How should the environment be managed and who should be responsible? What is effective environmental management, and for whom? These questions are answered by exploring traditional and emerging theoretical frameworks and applying them to real world environmental challenges.

title: Principles of Economics for Planning and Policy
description: Provides an introduction into economics for planning and policy students.

title: Urban Design Principles
description: Introduction to principles of urban design and its applications. Study of contemporary and traditional theories of urban design formulated to improve physical characteristics of built environment to facilitate an enhanced quality of life. A variety of case studies are discussed.

title: Urban Politics and Policy
description: Examines why and how urban policies are enacted and carried out in contemporary U.S. cities and regions. Topics include evolution and organization of city governments and policymaking over the past century; who directs public policy and controls how cities develop.

title: Public Policy and Governance
description: Exposes students to best practices that assure effective planning and implementation of policies and programs in government, business, and nonprofit sectors. Includes guest lecturers who are proven leaders in four principal institutions of community: business, education, government, and non-profit.

title: Health Policy
description: Considers social and economic aspects of health and disease in the United States. What are the proper roles of the individual, community, and government in improving health and health care? International comparisons will be made wherever possible.

title: Latino Metropolis
description: Explores the processes of Latino urbanization in the United States and the spatialization of Latino identities, particularly in the context of Southern California with selected comparisons drawing from other cities.

title: International Divided Cities
description: Investigates urban divisions in international cities where deep-seated nationalistic ethnic differences create pressures for intergroup conflicts, autonomy, or territorial separation, and can incite violence. Urban political polarization as it is manifest in the urban setting.

title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 13

title: History and Theory of Urban Planning
description: Introduces students to the historical bases, fundamental perspectives, and current challenges of urban and regional planning. Critical historical episodes and personalities in planning and their influences on contemporary planning practice and thought are explored.

title: Theoretical Foundations of Planning
description: Intellectual excursion into central themes in policy and planning, including philosophy of the market, institutionalization of space, hypostatizations of policy, constructions of communities, logics of spatial analysis. Objective is engagement of the professional in thoughtful reflections on practice and institutions.

title: Plan Development and Communication
description: Graphic representation and communication of physical place characteristics, design and physical planning ideas, and concepts using a variety of graphic techniques of free hand drawing, sketching, orthographic representations, scale drawings, 3D representations, maps, photo-documentation, and various media.

title: Microeconomic Analysis for Urban Planning
description: Provides students with a working knowledge of basic microeconomic concepts. Emphasizes applications related to urban planning and policy analysis. Topics covered include demand analysis, firm behavior, market structure, public goods, externalities, and the role of economics in land markets.

title: Land-Use Law
description: Investigates legal and institutional frameworks for development control. Review of constitutional issues implicated in land-use regulation. Traces development control historically and analyzes contemporary approaches to land-use control which reflect environmental and economic development concerns.

title: Qualitative Research Methods: Overview
description: Introduction to fundamentals of “qualitative” research and non-positivistic inquiry. Formulation of research questions, selection of method, data collection techniques, and analysis (briefly). Overview of selected methods from ethnography, naturalistic field research, phenomenology, ethnoarchaeology, critical approaches, and others.

title: Practice Experience
description: Provides Master of Urban and Regional Planning students an opportunity to link classroom knowledge with real planning situations through a 10-week unpaid practice experience.

title: Transportation Planning and Policy
description: Introduces current topics in transportation planning. Includes an analysis of the economic role of transportation in urban areas, land-use impacts of transportation projects, traffic congestion, air quality, alternatives to the automobile, and other transportation topics.
